claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 18 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as full-time non-advanced education, A-levels, Scottish Highers, or an approved training course)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 18 and studying A-levels, he may still be eligible as Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 who are in approved education.

Could you tell me if you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you! And just to confirm - are you responsible for Alex? In other words, do you live with him and/or pay at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me at home and I provide for all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He's just focused on his studies at the moment - no job and no benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Even though Alex is 18, Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 who are in approved education or training. Since Alex is studying A-levels at sixth form college, this counts as approved education. You live in the UK, Alex lives at home with you, you're responsible for him and provide for his needs, no one else is claiming for him, and he hasn't started full-time work (24+ hours per week) or claimed benefits in his own right.

You meet all the eligibility criteria, so you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex while he continues his studies.

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
